question.text: Mr. Vikram Singh, Manager of 'Deccan Capital' Cat II AIF, negotiates a Tag-Along Right on the founder's shares in investee 'Priya AgriTech Pvt Ltd'. The primary rationale for this right is:

answer.text: To force the founder to continuously reinvest dividends
To obtain a priority dividend distribution for the next 5 years
To prevent the founder from raising any new equity rounds
To ensure that if the founder sells shares, the AIF can also sell an equivalent percentage to the same buyer at the same price and terms

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.6.6 (Exit Rights), a tag-along (co-sale) right ensures that if a shareholder (typically the founder) sells shares, other shareholders can insist the buyer also purchase an equivalent percentage of their shares at the same price and terms. Rationale: AIF investors rely on founder commitment, so founder exit should drag minority investors along for liquidity. The Trap: Option A (reinvest dividends) is unrelated. Option C prevents all equity raises (too restrictive). Option D (priority dividend) is a separate liquidation-preference concept. Cross-Exam Context: Tag-along vs drag-along tested in XIX-A, XXI-B, and XV in deal-closing contexts. Manager's Pro-Tip: Standard tag-along is on a pari-passu basis. If the founder gets a control premium (say 25% over last round valuation), ensure the tag-along language captures that same premium — otherwise you tag at the lower market price.
